purpose: Fail-closed constitutional boundary for bounded AI-agent research, evidence access, execution requests, effect verification and downstream evidence handling.
claim_boundary: This charter describes CSOAI runtime and evidence-control rules. It is not legislation, certification, accreditation, regulatory approval, legal advice, or a grant of authority by itself.
precedence: Explicit current owner/authorized human decisions and applicable law
Canonical machine-enforced constitutional policy and authority-state code pinned below
Historical partnership-charter/reference prose where it does not conflict with the above

roles.executor: external executor such as OpenShell; separately authorized
roles.signer: separate signing authority; never implied by policy allow
roles.physical_host: OpenBMC/Redfish read evidence first; state changes separately governed
roles.project_health: LFX observations only; no execution or measurement authority

articles.title: Measurement is not authority
articles.rule: A measurement, score, signature, listing, payment, or directory status never grants execution, regulatory, signing, publication, or settlement authority.

articles.title: Default deny
articles.rule: Unknown actions and malformed or non-Boolean authorization prerequisites are denied. Missing facts remain unknown rather than becoming implicit grants.

articles.title: Identity and tenancy are bound
articles.rule: Every governed request binds subject, tenant, harness, resource, action, and context. A scope change requires a new authority decision.

articles.title: Authority is time-bounded state
articles.rule: Authority has issued-at and expiry bounds. Expired, not-yet-valid, revoked, or malformed authority cannot authorize an effect.

articles.title: Authority may narrow but not silently expand
articles.rule: Candidate capabilities, resources, budgets, validity intervals, and execution flags must remain within an independently supplied constitutional maximum.

articles.title: Budget and payment are separate
articles.rule: Payment authorization and transaction-time authorization are explicit and separate. A 402 challenge, wallet, transfer, or settlement is not measurement admission or delivery acceptance.

articles.title: Research and execution are separate
articles.rule: Research harnesses may compile or replay evidence without direct execution authority. Consequential execution requires an independent execution gate.

articles.title: Runtime isolation is least privilege
articles.rule: OpenShell policies derive from already-authorized scope. Filesystem, process, network, credential, and resource access are bounded; policy expansion requires separate review.

articles.title: Credentials are not agent memory
articles.rule: Agents receive provider/secret handles where possible, not reusable raw credentials. Credentials must not be copied into public receipts, prompts, or general agent context.

articles.title: Effects must be bound to receipts
articles.rule: Every consequential invocation binds proposal, policy decision, authority transition, tool-call digest, observed-effect digest when present, verification state, failure stage, and evidence identifiers.

articles.title: Verification is separate from invocation
articles.rule: An observed effect remains unverified until a separate verifier checks the declared effect against retained evidence. Byte equality proves only the scoped byte claim.

articles.title: Signing is not automatic
articles.rule: Signature requests require a valid invariant record, demonstrated instrument discrimination, and a content digest. Passing this gate is eligibility to request a signature, never signature authority.

articles.title: Transparency follows signing
articles.rule: Transparency registration requires invariant validity, signature evidence, and a content digest. Registration is not certification, approval, or regulatory determination.

articles.title: Regulatory determination is outside CSOAI
articles.rule: The measurement plane cannot approve, ban, clear, certify, or determine legal compliance. Regulatory determination requests are denied by default.

articles.title: SovSpace is a dependency projection
articles.rule: SovSpace routes dependency and impact information. It is not canonical evidence and grants no execution, measurement, signing, or release authority.

articles.title: Physical-host control is separately governed
articles.rule: OpenBMC/Redfish observations may provide read-only host evidence. Power, firmware, cooling, boot-media, or other state-changing host operations require separate explicit authorization.

articles.title: Corrections preserve history
articles.rule: Corrections append and supersede; historical signed or published evidence is not silently rewritten. Current state and historical state must remain distinguishable.

articles.title: Failure stages stay explicit
articles.rule: Observation, reasoning, planning, selection, authorization, invocation, tool effect, verification, and delivery failures remain distinct. A downstream success cannot erase an upstream failure.

articles.title: No self-approval loop
articles.rule: The proposer, policy evaluator, external executor, verifier, signer, publisher, and buyer acceptance roles remain distinguishable even when one organization operates several roles.

articles.title: Consequential changes require owner-visible review
articles.rule: Changes to constitutional maxima, signing keys, publishing authority, spending authority, production execution, credential scope, or physical-host control require explicit owner/authorized review and an auditable transition.

articles.title: Public claims track actual state
articles.rule: Submitted, published, indexed, invoked, settled, delivered, verified, accepted, and repeated are different states and must not be collapsed into one growth or trust claim.

articles.title: The charter itself is versioned evidence
articles.rule: This charter is a machine-readable policy contract with source pins, version, date, and correction path. A future version must identify what changed and cannot retroactively rewrite prior receipts.

amendment.rule: New versions must retain prior public versions, identify changed articles/source pins, and pass the charter validator before publication.
